note: *derramou-se a graça nos teus lábios*, verb first so the antiphon *Diffúsa est grátia* stands alone. The stylist said verb-first sounds translated and asked *nos teus lábios se derramou a graça*, option 2.

*atende*, D3's verb for the absolute *inténde*; the blind reader heard "pay attention", odd before *avança*. It waits on D40 (HANDOFF 22). *estende o arco* (the Greek) and *põe-te a caminho* (DRB) are options.
The psalm says *tu* to king and bride (rule 3; D17 left it here), which gives *O teu trono, ó Deus*. The blind reader heard a turn to God. The whole *vós* text is option 2 (HANDOFF 22).
*ansiará pelo teu esplendor*, held against two Latinist minors asking *formosura*, which is *spécies*' word in 44:5a. The stylist found *ansiará* stiff; *desejar* is *desideráre*'s.
